title: How can one number show the date you picked?
description: {{NAME_2}} follows the date trick with the twenty sixth of January and reports two hundred ninety one. The steps are then done with letters for the month and the day, and {{NAME_1}} reads the date back. Keeko doubts that the day is just the last two digits of the answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: the steps turn the date into one hundred em plus a fixed number plus dee, so the fixed number comes off first. Watch for students who read the last two digits of the answer before taking the fixed number away.

source: Mukta thinks of 26 January and follows the steps. Show that
video_script.why: A child sees that the date trick builds one hundred times the month plus a fixed number plus the day, so taking the fixed number away gives the date back.
video_script.substitution: the book's own date trick with the twenty sixth of January, then the letters em and dee
video_script.anchor: the date trick card: multiply the month by 5, add 6, multiply by 4, add 9, multiply by 5, add the day
video_script.wrong_move: reads the last two digits of the answer as the day, without taking the fixed 165 away first
video_script.payoff_line: Subtract one hundred sixty five, and the date reads off as the twenty sixth of January.

names.{{NAME_1}}: the friend who reads the date back from the answer
names.{{NAME_2}}: the friend who thinks of the date and follows the steps

hold_back: subtract 165 and the date reads off
maths_rules: With letters: 5M, then 5M + 6, then 20M + 24, then 20M + 33, then 100M + 165, then 100M + 165 + D.
291 - 165 = 126, which is 100M + D, so M = 1 and D = 26.
A day is at most 31, so D needs only the last two digits.
video_script.design: One idea: the trick builds one hundred em plus a fixed number plus dee. The trick card stays in the anchor band and the number try sits above the letter try on the working board.

beats.on_screen: the small title card From your book appears; {{NAME_2}} and {{NAME_1}} face each other; the date trick card shows six steps and a closed date box; a slip with the answer 291 is written in the anchor band

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.steps: the six step cards line up and a closed date box appears
marks.ask: the slip with the answer 291 appears and the question is written

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book. {{NAME_2}} thinks of a date, and {{NAME_1}} gives six steps to follow.
<bookmark mark='steps'/>{{NAME_2}} follows the steps with a secret date and says only the answer.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The answer is two hundred ninety one. How can {{NAME_1}} read the date from it?

beats.on_screen: the answer slip 291 holds still and the question glows

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two boxes labelled M for the month and D for the day; the words day at most 31, two digits are written under D

marks.letters: the boxes M and D appear
marks.two: the words day at most 31, two digits appear under D

narration: <bookmark mark='letters'/>Let the month be em and the day be dee.
<bookmark mark='two'/>A day is at most thirty one, so it fits in two digits.

beats.on_screen: Given: month × 5; + 6; × 4; + 9; × 5; + the day; date 26 January
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the steps start with the month. Multiply by five, add six, multiply by four, add nine, multiply by five, and add the day.
<bookmark mark='date'/>The date is the twenty sixth of January.

beats.on_screen: To find: the answer of the trick, and how the date is read back

marks.find: the things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to show the answer is two hundred ninety one. We also find how the date is read back.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, the month is one. One times five is five, and five plus six is eleven.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Eleven times four is forty four, and forty four plus nine is fifty three.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Fifty three times five is two hundred sixty five. Adding the day twenty six gives two hundred ninety one.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Step two, do the same with letters. Em times five is five em, and adding six gives five em plus six.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Multiply by four to get twenty em plus twenty four. Add nine to get twenty em plus thirty three.
<bookmark mark='five2'/>Multiply by five to get one hundred em plus one hundred sixty five, and add the day dee.

marks.split: 126 = 100M + D is written with the last two digits 26 boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step three, take away one hundred sixty five from two hundred ninety one. That leaves one hundred twenty six.
<bookmark mark='split'/>That is one hundred em plus dee, and the day uses only the last two digits.
<bookmark mark='read'/>The day is twenty six and the month is one, which is the twenty sixth of January.

beats.on_screen: Answer: subtract 165 and the date reads off: 26 January
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Subtract one hundred sixty five, and the date reads off as the twenty sixth of January.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the day is 91, from the last two digits of 291; a calendar page with at most 31 days appears; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble the day is 91 appears
marks.cal: a calendar page with at most 31 days appears beside it
marks.strike: the fixed 165 flashes and the bubble is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the day is ninety one, reading the last two digits of the answer.
<bookmark mark='cal'/>No month has more than thirty one days.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The steps added a fixed one hundred sixty five, and it must come off first.
